novelty_basis: Implicit in the linear-algebra proof of the upper bound of A. Cusenza et al., Bounds on Zeckendorf games, Fibonacci Quart. 60 (2022), arXiv:2009.09510 (Thm 1.3), and used as an inequality step ('subtract the excess MC2 + 2MC3 + ...') in J. Cheigh et al., Towards the Gaussianity of random Zeckendorf games, CANT VI, Springer 2025, doi 10.1007/978-3-031-65064-2_4. The one-line potential proof is ours.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C19.md Theorem 1; potential Psi(c) = sum c_i a_i); the per-move changes of Psi and their sum over an arbitrary move list are Lean-verified (dPsi_C1, dPsi_S2, dPsi_split, dPsi_combine, length_identity; standard axioms only); checked on all greedy games n < 1500 and 1500 random games (EXP-C19-02)
statement:
For every game G on n (from n copies of F_1 to the Zeckendorf representation), |G| = B(n) - sum_{i>=2} (i-1) MC_i(G),
where B(n) = sum_i (F_{i+2} - i - 2) delta_i is the bound of Cusenza et al. and MC_i counts the combines
F_{i-1} + F_i -> F_{i+1}. Hence a game is longest iff it minimises the weighted number of such combines, and
L(n) = B(n) - D(n) with D(n) = min_G sum (i-1) MC_i(G).
title: Every Zeckendorf game has length B(n) - sum_{i>=2} (i-1) MC_i
